🔥 Maya says it at the fire, not quite looking at Stan: “Your past story doesn’t add up. Someone had to say it.” The fire goes quiet in the way it does when someone’s decided to be brave.
“You’re right.” Stan doesn’t look up. “I wasn’t Denver. I was Chicago, Illinois. I’m sorry — I wanted a cleaner story than I had.” The fire lets it land. Someone passes Stan the bowl without a word.
People bring you their suspicions, written down. You keep every one.
Isabella Goycochea reads the sky: rain tomorrow, cold.
